function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • **Single pane of glass** that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards with AI‑driven anomaly detection. | Unilever can see the health of its global supply‑chain, marketing, and retail workloads in one place, reducing blind spots that siloed native tools create. | | **Predictive Capacity Planning** | • Uses machine‑learning models to forecast CPU, memory, I/O, and network usage 24–48 h ahead.
• Suggests right‑size resources before performance degrades. | Enables Unilever to avoid over‑provisioning (cost) or under‑provisioning (service outages) across its multi‑cloud portfolio. | | **Automated Remediation & Optimization** | • AI recommends or automatically applies changes (e.g., scaling, re‑allocation, spot‑instance usage).
• Integrates with Terraform, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines. | Reduces manual toil for Unilever’s ops teams and ensures workloads run at optimal cost/performance. | | **Business‑Driven SLAs** | • Maps business KPIs (e.g., order‑to‑delivery time, marketing campaign latency) to technical metrics.
• Generates alerts when business impact thresholds are breached. | Aligns IT operations with Unilever’s commercial objectives, not just technical ones. | | **Cross‑Cloud Cost Transparency** | • Consolidates billing data from all clouds into a single cost model.
• AI identifies waste, idle resources, and cost‑saving opportunities. | Gives Unilever a clear view of where money is spent and where savings can be realized. | | **Governance & Compliance** | • Enforces policies (e.g., data residency, security controls) across clouds.
• AI flags policy violations in real time. | Helps Unilever meet regulatory requirements (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) while operating globally. | #### How It Works in Practice 1. **Data Collection** – Turbonomics pulls telemetry from cloud APIs, Kubernetes metrics, and on‑prem monitoring agents. 2. **AI Engine** – A proprietary ML model ingests the telemetry, learns normal patterns, and flags anomalies. 3. **Decision Layer** – Business rules (e.g., “if latency > 200 ms, scale up by 20%”) are applied. 4. **Action Layer** – The platform issues API calls to the respective cloud provider or orchestrator to enact changes. 5. **Feedback Loop** – Outcomes are fed back into the model to improve future predictions. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Tools (GCP, AWS, Azure) | Feature | Turbonomics | Native Cloud Tool (e.g., GCP Operations, AWS CloudWatch, Azure Monitor) | |---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------| | **Scope** | **Multi‑cloud + hybrid** – works across all major clouds and on‑prem. | **Single‑cloud** – limited to the provider’s own environment. | | **Observability Depth** | Aggregates *all* resource types (VMs, containers, databases, networking, storage) into unified dashboards. | Focuses on provider‑specific services; often requires stitching multiple dashboards manually. | | **AI/ML Capabilities** | Built‑in predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and automated remediation. | Basic alerting and dashboards; advanced AI usually requires separate services (e.g., AWS Lookout for Metrics, Azure AI). | | **Cost Optimization** | Unified cost model, cross‑cloud optimization recommendations, spot‑instance management. | Native cost tools provide per‑service cost insights but lack cross‑cloud comparison or automated optimization. | | **Policy & Governance** | Central policy engine that spans all clouds; AI flags violations. | Policies are provider‑specific; governance across clouds requires custom tooling. | | **Automation** | API‑first, integrates with Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, CI/CD. | Automation is possible but often fragmented; each provider has its own set of APIs and tooling. | | **Learning Curve** | One learning curve for the Turbonomics UI and API. | Multiple learning curves—one per cloud provider. | | **Vendor Lock‑In** | Vendor‑agnostic; no lock‑in to a single cloud. | Inherent lock‑in to the chosen cloud provider. | #### Bottom Line - **Turbonomics** gives Unilever a *single, AI‑powered lens* that cuts through the complexity of managing workloads across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on‑prem. - **Native tools** are powerful within their own ecosystems but require significant effort to stitch together for a coherent, cross‑cloud view. By adopting Turbonomics, Unilever can: - Reduce operational overhead and manual toil. - Achieve tighter alignment between IT performance and business outcomes. - Unlock cost savings that native tools alone would miss. - Maintain flexibility to shift workloads between clouds without being locked into a single vendor’s ecosystem.
